**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity).**

**What I found.** Section 7.2 (p0026) provides: *"Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives."* Although the document contains no clause using the word "exclusive" against us, this sentence functions as a right of first refusal / de facto exclusivity: we cannot engage another supplier without first surfacing the competing terms to Cobalt and giving it the chance to match. It is unlimited as to product category, runs for the full three-year term, and has no performance-based exit — squarely the walk-away scenario, and well short of the fallback (defined category, 12 months, automatic termination on service-level or delivery failure).

**Supporting context.** Section 12.3 (p0044) expressly states that Vendor acknowledges Customer "has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment," so 7.2 is also internally inconsistent with the agreement's own no-restriction provision. Deleting 7.2 reaches the preferred position and removes the conflict.

**Scope discipline.** I did not flag Section 13.1's non-exclusive licence or Section 14.2's ownership language (not supplier-freedom restrictions), nor Section 2.1's volume commitment or Section 12.4's non-compete, which belong to other rules. The most-favoured-pricing dimension of the same sentence is left to the MFN rule to avoid double-flagging the same commercial term.

**Redline validated (ok:true):** delete p0026, with a comment offering the category/12-month/performance-exit fallback if Cobalt needs something in its place.
